appraisal_events.evidence: "elle lui en donnait maintenant si peu qu'il était obligé de considérer comme telles les défenses qu'elle lui faisait d'une chose ou d'une autre"; Swann tells Charlus "je crois pourtant qu'elle m'aime; elle est si gentille pour moi" after obeying her caprice about his coachman.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator exposes Swann's self-deceiving logic: because Odette gives him so little real affection, he is reduced to reading her trivial complaints and arbitrary demands (dismissing his coachman) as proof of love, and his confident declaration to Charlus is framed ironically by this preceding exposition.

status_effects.explanation: Swann is shown as emotionally dependent and self-deceiving, forced to manufacture proofs of love from Odette's trivial complaints and to comply with her whims (dismissing his own coachman) in order to sustain his belief that she cares for him.
Odette exercises effective, unquestioned leverage over Swann's household arrangements even while giving little affection in return, locally reinforcing her control over him.
